steps.title: Prepare E3 medium (1 L)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.2922 g NaCl, 0.0126465 g KCl, 48.51 mg CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 81.3351 mg MgSO₄·7H₂O in deionized water, add 200 µL methylene‑blue solution (0.002 % final), and bring the volume to 1 L with deionized water.

steps.title: Prepare 10× PTU stock (0.03 %)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.03 g PTU, dissolve in deionized water and bring the volume to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS
steps.instruction: Measure 100 mL deionized water at ~25 °C, add one PBS tablet (pH 7.4), stir until fully dissolved; do not use water warmer than 25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare embryo lysis buffer (10 mL)
steps.instruction: Combine 1 mL 10× PCR gold buffer, 30 µL NP‑40 (to give 0.3 % v/v total), 30 µL Tween 20 (0.3 % v/v total), and add deionized water up to 10 mL.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Mix 2.5 mL 10× PCR gold buffer, 0.5 mL 10 mM dNTP mix (2.5 mM each dNTP), 1.5 mL 25 mM MgCl₂ solution, and 17.38 mL deionized water (total 22 mL). Aliquot and store at –20 °C for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Set up zebrafish cross
steps.instruction: Fill clean breeding tanks with system water, select healthy heterozygous adult pairs, place male and female in the tank separated by a mating divider in the evening, keep under a 14 h light/10 h dark cycle, and remove the divider the next morning when lights turn on; monitor for mating and eggs.

steps.title: Collect embryos
steps.instruction: When eggs appear at the tank bottom, net out the adults to a new tank, pour the embryos through a mesh strainer, rinse gently with E3 medium using a squeeze bottle to remove debris, transfer embryos to a 10 cm Petri dish containing 15 mL E3 medium, and incubate at 28.5 °C with a 14 h light/10 h dark cycle. Clean and disinfect tanks and nets after each use.

steps.title: Embryo care and PTU treatment
steps.instruction: Monitor development, discard unfertilized or unhealthy embryos, and at ~10 h post‑fertilization (gastrulation) add 5 mL of the 10× PTU stock to 50 mL E3 medium (final PTU 0.003 %) to inhibit pigment formation (optional if pigment does not interfere). Maintain embryos until the desired collection timepoint.

steps.title: Optional embryo fixation
steps.instruction: Fix embryos in 4 % PFA at 4 °C overnight, replace with 1 % PFA the next morning, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Genomic DNA isolation – buffer distribution
steps.instruction: Dispense 50 µL embryo lysis buffer into individual PCR tubes, 8‑strip tubes, or 96‑well plates according to the number of samples.

steps.title: Collect tissue samples
steps.instruction: Choose one method: (a) Dechorionate live embryos, anesthetize with 0.02 % tricaine, cut tail, and place tail in 50 µL lysis buffer; (b) Anesthetize adult fish with 0.016 % tricaine, clip a small portion of the tail fin, and place in 50 µL lysis buffer; (c) For 4 % PFA‑fixed embryos, cut tails, transfer to 1× PBS, wash 3 × 5 min, then move to 50 µL lysis buffer. Decontaminate forceps with 70 % ethanol between each embryo.

steps.title: Lysis and proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 98 °C for 10 min then 4 °C for 2 min; add 5 µL proteinase K (10 mg/mL) to each tube, mix, and incubate at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Proteinase K inactivation and DNA recovery
steps.instruction: Next day, heat at 98 °C for 10 min then 4 °C for 5 min, centrifuge at 1 500 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, and transfer 40 µL supernatant to a fresh PCR tube (store at –20 °C if not used immediately).

steps.title: Set up PCR reaction
steps.instruction: For each sample combine 19 µL PCR master mix, 0.04 µL forward primer (100 mM), 0.04 µL reverse primer (100 mM), 0.015 µL AmpliTaq Gold DNA polymerase, and 1 µL genomic DNA template. Prepare a master mix (all components except template) for multiple reactions to reduce pipetting error.

steps.title: Run PCR cycling
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler: initial denaturation 96 °C 6 min; 45 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, annealing at the primer‑specific temperature *°C for 30 s, extension 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 7 min; hold at 4 °C for 3 min, then at 15 °C. Adjust annealing temperature as needed; conditions are optimized for AmpliTaq Gold but can be adapted for other polymerases.

steps.title: Check PCR product on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL of each PCR product onto a 4 % agarose gel and run 80 min at 150 V; visualize bands to confirm amplification.

steps.title: Restriction digestion of PCR product
steps.instruction: In a tube mix 10 µL PCR product, 0.1 µL MboII enzyme, 2 µL 10× (L) buffer, and 3 µL Milli‑Q water (total 15.1 µL). Incubate according to the enzyme’s recommended temperature and time (typically 37 °C for 30 min).

steps.title: Resolve digested products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL of the restriction‑digested reaction onto a 4 % agarose gel and run 80 min at 150 V; the pattern distinguishes wild‑type, heterozygous, and homozygous genotypes.

steps.title: Toluidine‑blue staining of sections (optional)
steps.instruction: Dechorionate embryos, fix in 4 % PFA at 4 °C overnight, wash 3 × 5 min with 1× PBS at room temperature, dehydrate through ethanol series (30 % 2 min, 50 % 2 min, 70 % 2 min, 100 % twice 2 min each), transfer to 1:1 100 % ethanol:JB‑4 solution A for 3 h at room temperature, then immerse in JB‑4 solution A overnight at 4 °C. Embed in JB‑4 A + B mixed 25:1 in a rectangular silicone mold, cover with cellophane paper, let solidify, trim, mount on a 2 cm wooden block, section 5–7 µm with a microtome, place sections on water domes on glass slides, dry on a hot plate, dip briefly in 0.1 % toluidine‑blue solution, wash with distilled water until excess dye is removed, dry on hot plate, mount with inclusion reagent, and image under a microscope.

description: Validation of protocol Electrophoresis of PCR-amplified DNAs in an agarose gel to distinguish genotypes: wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous mutants To validate the PCR-based genotyping method, genomic DNA from zebrafish embryos ( banp rw337 ) was amplified using specifically designed primers (forward: 5′-CGATGTTGATATCCATCAGTCAGGCGATC-3′; reverse primer: 5′-GGTGCTGGTGTATAAATCACATGACCTATGGTCCTCTT-3′) and subjected to restriction enzyme digestion using MboII. The resulting PCR products were analyzed by electrophoresis on a 4% agarose gel to distinguish wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous mutant embryos. This validation step confirms the reliability of the genotyping protocol in differentiating genetic variants based on their banding patterns. As shown in Figure 4 , wild-type embryos display a single upper band at 239 bp, homozygous mutants exhibit a single lower band at 212 bp, and heterozygous embryos present both bands at 212 and 239 bp. Furthermore, to confirm the genotypes at the tissue morphology level, toluidine blue staining was performed on sectioned embryos. As illustrated in Figure 5 , differences in tissue structure between wild-type and mutant embryos were evident, with mutant embryos displaying pyknotic cells indicative of cell death. These results demonstrate that PCR amplification, restriction digestion, and subsequent histological analysis effectively identify zebrafish genotypes at early developmental stages. Figure 4. Genotyping of 20 embryos produced by banp rw337 heterozygous parent fishes.
